Build lessons this round (kept because each cost a run)

  • A validator's CLI block ran on import. The receipt tool imported check() and the validator parsed its argv, trying to open a file named make. A module that is both a library and a CLI must guard the CLI with an entry-point check.

  • A subclass of a frozen object cannot add own properties (World freezes its instances); module-private state keyed by a WeakMap is the honest "inside the boundary" representation.

  • Audit the anchors before the run: walking the build with ast and counting every literal / regex anchor in the v2.7 documents found the only mismatch in one pass — one refusal per run is the expensive way.

  • A mutation must run where its defect is reachable: the v2.7-rule mutation on STRICT + NAIVE showed nothing, because that reconciler never learns satisfaction; on KEY-ONLY + NAIVE it reintroduced the avoidable duplicate. The same fact became an expectation ("revalidation needs a far side that can say satisfied").

  • The gate caught five phrases my own edits left (two version-history sentences still calling F36/F37 unadjudicated; "candidate for PROVED"; the typo phrase quoted verbatim, which is itself the forbidden phrase; one promotions without the rename wording). Fixed in the build, never by hand in the package.
